intent: squash-merge the base PR in a stacked 3-branch series and rebase dependent branches onto the new main without closing them

relevant.why: Squash-merging the base PR from inside a linked worktree requires using `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{N}/merge -f merge_method=squash` — `gh pr merge --squash --delete-branch` fails with 'main is already used by worktree', which is a normal condition in stacked-PR workflows where the primary checkout holds main.

After running `gh pr merge` from a linked worktree, the merge succeeds on GitHub but the local checkout step fails non-zero; the agent must verify actual merge success via `gh pr view --json state,mergedAt` before proceeding to rebase dependent branches.

Before rebasing dependent branches onto the updated main, `git fetch origin && git pull origin main` is required; the rule also flags that a parallel PR could have already landed overlapping changes, making some rebased hunks redundant — directly relevant to the rebase step in a stacked series.

If local main is ahead of origin after the squash-merge (e.g. due to hook commits), rebasing dependent branches onto it produces a polluted diff on their PRs; confirming local main matches origin before rebasing avoids this.

intent: update existing Go tests that fail after adding a new required validation field to a CLI command

relevant.why: Directly addresses adding new lifecycle values/validation guards to shared valid-sets in Go: put all cross-field invariants in the shared validate() function, trace every command that reaches the new member, and add the guard there rather than per-command — exactly what is needed when a new required validation field is added to a CLI command.

Directly addresses both: (1) consolidating duplicated value-whitelist functions that may exist across packages after a validation change, and (2) centralizing hard-coded absolute-count assertions in shared test fixtures so that adding a new validation member requires only one fixture change rather than hunting across many test files.

When updating tests after a required validation field is added, the internal validation function signature may change; this rule advises restricting tests to the exported public API so they compile and pass both before and after the fix — prevents a class of test-update failures where tests break on internal renames.

If the test fixture updates involve creating or modifying files under testdata/, the repo-wide **/testdata/ gitignore rule silently excludes them from commits, causing CI to fail on clean checkouts while local tests pass — directly relevant when adding new fixture inputs for the new required field.

Contains the advice to run the full integration-test suite after any schema field or config key change because doctor/validate commands embed field-name strings as literals that silently become stale — marginally applicable when a new required validation field is added to a CLI command.

intent: add a quickstart command to the autosearch CLI that outputs agent-oriented markdown

relevant.why: Adding a new Cobra subcommand must use NewXxxCmd() constructor pattern (not package-level *cobra.Command vars) to avoid test-harness panics; also flags for a quickstart command should default correctly per ACs.

After implementing the quickstart command, must run make check / golangci-lint run ./... before declaring done — go build and go test alone are insufficient gates.
Quickstart outputs agent-oriented markdown to stdout; any errors or diagnostics must go to stderr. The rule enforces keeping stdout strictly clean for CLI tool output.

If the quickstart markdown constant or helper function is defined separately from the newQuickstartCmd() registration, both must land in the same commit to avoid unused-symbol lint failures from the pre-commit hook.
Before scripting 'auto search quickstart' in plan steps or ACs, the exact subcommand name must be verified via --help to avoid plan steps referencing non-existent surfaces.

intent: tag a new minor version release and verify GitHub Actions release workflow builds all monorepo binaries

relevant.why: Before tagging a release, local main must be fully in sync with origin. This monorepo's pre-commit hook and dogfooding daemon routinely advance main between sessions; tagging from a local main that is ahead of origin can place the tag on an un-pushed commit, meaning GitHub Actions never sees it or sees the wrong tree. The rule's explicit `git fetch origin && git push origin main` sync check directly applies.

Complementary git-sync discipline: run `git fetch origin && git pull origin main` before branching or tagging to avoid a stale base. For release tagging, being behind origin means tagging an old commit and publishing a release from outdated code.

When verifying that the release workflow builds ALL monorepo binaries, this rule warns that Go modules absent from PROJECTS in the aggregate Makefile are silently excluded from every CI quality gate. If the release workflow drives off the same Makefile targets, an unregistered module would be quietly missing from the binary matrix.

intent: add a new metadata field to autodoc frontmatter and thread it through fix, stale, and agents commands

relevant.why: Hard tool invariant: must Read every file (frontmatter.go, stale.go, fixed.go, agents.go, doctree.go) before editing. The schema is spread across multiple files that all need reading first.

Threading a new field through fix, stale, and agents means adding helpers (e.g. updated Parse/Serialize/ComputeHash) before their callers in the command layer. Committing helpers without callers breaks the pre-commit unused-symbol lint gate.

Adding a frontmatter field is a schema field change. The rule explicitly states: 'after renaming any schema field or config key, run the full integration-test suite before committing, because doctor/validate commands embed field-name strings as literals that silently become stale' — exactly the stale/fix command risk here.

CheckStale has an inline required-field guard (`e.Title == "" || e.Summary == "" || e.ReadWhen == ""`). Adding a new required field means updating this guard; the rule warns against maintaining parallel validation copies across packages rather than a single shared check.

Cross-field invariants (required fields, presence constraints) should live in a shared validate() function, not scattered per-command. Adding a new required frontmatter field risks putting the presence check only in CheckStale, not in fix, agents, or a shared validator.

When threading a field through multiple files across fix, stale, and agents, each intermediate commit must pass `make check` / golangci-lint, not just `go build` or `go test`, to avoid accumulating lint debt that surfaces at the final gate.

If the new field is a computed or bookkeeping value (e.g. an embedding hash, agent usage count), this rule warns not to embed it inline in doc files — externalize to a sidecar instead. The inline `hash` field already sets precedent; extending the pattern to another computed field amplifies the 'mechanical rewrite' problem.

Applies to any Go implementation phase: must run golangci-lint (not just go build/vet/test) as a verify gate — linters like modernize and nilerr surface real defects that standard tooling skips.

intent: run autoetl pipeline then rebuild autosearch index before querying session history

relevant.why: Directly on-point: when running a full ETL rebuild, --full must delete ALL incremental state including external sync-state files (e.g. ~/.auto/etl/git/sync-state.json), not just the output directory — otherwise seen-SHA sets remain intact and the run silently produces zero new rows, indistinguishable from a successful incremental run.

autoetl runs multiple sub-sources (codex, claude, git, etc.); a 404 or failure in one unrelated sub-source causes the whole command to exit non-zero even if the target sessions transform succeeded — knowing to use --only <source> or interpret per-source exit status is essential before concluding the pipeline failed.

Orphaned parquet partitions from abandoned branches or schema changes cause DuckDB to NULL-fill silently across partitions; if the autosearch index rebuild reads cross-partition drift, a --full backfill of ETL output may be required before the index reflects accurate data.

The causal note explicitly calls out 'autoetl transform' being wrong while the real command surface is 'autoetl run'; verifying exact subcommand names with --help before scripting the ETL→index→query workflow prevents silent failures from non-existent subcommands.

When querying session history after rebuilding the index, scoping by normalized git remote (not cwd/workspace path) is required in a worktree workflow — path-equality scoping fragments one repo's records into disjoint sets per worktree, silently missing the majority of sessions.
